# Ships drop minerals (AH-0MULUOZQP009GRWX)

## Problem statement

When a non-asteroid enemy that has absorbed minerals is destroyed, the game
re-drops a **floored fraction (25–50 %)** of what it absorbed. Because the
count is floored, an enemy that absorbed only one or two minerals drops
**nothing**, and the distribution under-rewards the player relative to the
intent. The re-drop should instead add a **random bonus of 0.25–1.25** to the
absorbed count and **round to the nearest integer**, so every destroyed
mineral-carrying enemy reliably returns roughly what it held (and may
occasionally return slightly more).

## Users

- **As a player**, when I destroy an enemy that has been hoovering up my
  minerals, I want it to release back about the minerals it absorbed (plus a
  small random bonus) so the effort to shoot it feels rewarded and
  predictable.
- **As a game designer**, I want the re-drop amount to stay a single
  configurable rule that the game and every gym consume, so the behaviour
  cannot drift between them.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **New formula** — `BaseEnemy.mineralRedropCount(rng)` returns
   `Math.round(collected + random(0.25, 1.25))`, where the bonus is drawn from
   the injected rng in `[0.25, 1.25]` (one draw). At the extremes,
   `rng() = 0` → `round(collected + 0.25)` and `rng() → 1` →
   `round(collected + 1.25)`.
   *Verification:* unit tests over several collected counts at both rng
   extremes.
2. **No upper cap** — the re-drop is no longer clamped to the collected count,
   so an enemy that absorbed `N` minerals may drop up to
   `round(N + 1.25)`, and never less than `round(N + 0.25)`.
   *Verification:* unit tests showing the upper bound exceeds `N` for
   `N = 1, 2` and the lower bound holds.
3. **Empty enemy unchanged** — an enemy that absorbed nothing still re-drops
   nothing (`mineralRedropCount` returns `0` when `mineralCount <= 0`).
   *Verification:* unit test.
4. **Shared rule preserved (game/gym parity)** — `resolveMineralKillDrops`
   (consumed by both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene`) spawns exactly
   `mineralRedropCount(rng)` scattered minerals at the death site with no
   divergent copy of the calculation.
   *Verification:* the shared-helper tests and the gym re-drop test are updated
   to the new rule; the repo-wide duplicate-body guard in
   `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` passes.
5. **Tunables renamed to match the new semantics** —
   `mineralRedropFractionMin/Max` become `mineralRedropBonusMin/Max`
   (defaults `0.25` / `1.25`), persisted and loaded with corrupt-value
   fallback; legacy persisted configs (schema v1/v2) migrate without carrying
   stale fraction values.
   *Verification:* `rules.test.ts` covers defaults, save/load round-trip,
   invalid-value fallback and legacy migration.
6. **Documentation updated** — the rule, the removed cap and the renamed
   tunables are reflected in GDD §4.1 E7 and §4.4.1, the module-tree entries
   and the README mineral section, plus the affected code/module comments.
   *Verification:* doc review; no remaining "25–50 %" claims for this rule.
7. **Full project test suite passes** with the new behaviour.
   *Verification:* run the full suite and all quality checks green.

## Constraints

- **UK English** in all written output.
- **Single shared implementation** — the calculation must stay in
  `BaseEnemy.mineralRedropCount` (reached through
  `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts`); the game and every gym must not gain
  a private copy (enforced by the repo-wide parity guard).
- **Testability** — `mineralRedropCount(rng)` keeps its injectable rng and one
  draw per call so seeded tests stay deterministic.
- **No new gameplay surface** — no changes to scatter radius, asteroid drops,
  collection, the hold or the HUD.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — `mineralRedropCount(rng)` computes
  `[floor(N × mineralRedropFractionMin), floor(N × mineralRedropFractionMax)]`
  (0.25/0.5) and draws an integer inside it, clamped to `N`.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` — the shared kill-drop rule; delegates
  the non-asteroid count to `BaseEnemy.mineralRedropCount` and the scatter to
  `scatterMineralDrops` (`src/entities/Mineral.ts`).
- `src/core/rules.ts` — `mineralRedropFractionMin/Max` = 0.25/0.5,
  `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2`, `coerceFraction` (range `[0, 1]`).
- Docs and tests assert the **25–50 %** rule and the **never-exceed** cap
  (`docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.1/§4.4.1, `README.md`,
  `BaseEnemy.minerals.test.ts`, `mineralKillDrops.test.ts`,
  `Harvester.test.ts`, `GymFormationScene.test.ts`, `rules.test.ts`).

## Desired change

- Replace the formula with `Math.round(collected + random(0.25, 1.25))` and
  drop the upper cap.
- Rename the tunables to `mineralRedropBonusMin/Max` with defaults
  0.25/1.25, bump the rules schema to v3 and migrate legacy configs, adding
  non-negative coercion suitable for the wider range.
- Update the shared-helper comments, tests and documentation to describe the
  additive bonus and nearest-integer rounding.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — new `mineralRedropCount` formula and updated
  JSDoc.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — renamed tunables, new defaults/constants, schema v3
  and migration/coercion.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` — rule description in the module
  header (logic unchanged; still delegates).
- `src/entities/__tests__/BaseEnemy.minerals.test.ts` — rewrite the re-drop
  distribution tests for the new formula and removed cap.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.test.ts` — update expected counts at the
  rng extremes.
- `src/entities/Harvester.test.ts` — update the Harvester re-drop test.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — update the non-asteroid
  re-drop test (remove the never-exceed assertion).
- `src/core/rules.test.ts` — defaults, round-trip, invalid fallback and legacy
  migration for the renamed tunables.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.1 E7, §4.4.1 and the module tree.
- `README.md` — mineral rule/tunable lines.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q** — *Asteroids drop collectable minerals…* (parent
  feature that introduced enemy absorption and re-drop).
- **AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB** — *Gym asteroids do not drop minerals — share the
  mineral kill-drop code with the game* (created the shared rule this change
  modifies).
- **AH-0MUCST3QD002O9TA** — *Mineral rules tunables and per-enemy mineral
  count* (introduced the tunables being renamed).
- **AH-0MUCST1P10004EXM** — *Test: Enemy mineral count and re-drop
  distribution* (the tests being updated).
- **AH-0MUJRVZP2002G8GC** — *Shared mineral-seek seam parity* (related shared
  mineral seam; completed).
- **AH-0MUCST4M7008O9CX** — *Pluggable power-up choice strategy and
  permanent-effect support* (adjacent mineral-hold/power-up path; completed).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the `mineralCount <= 0 → 0` guard is retained — a ship that
  absorbed nothing drops nothing, even though the bare formula would yield
  `0` or `1` at `N = 0`. Rationale: the requirement says it drops *the
  minerals it collected*, and the GDD already states "an enemy that collected
  nothing re-drops nothing".
- **Assumption:** the tunables are renamed to `mineralRedropBonusMin/Max`
  (defaults 0.25/1.25) rather than keeping the now-misleading
  `…Fraction…` names, with a schema bump to v3 and an explicit migration.
- **Risk:** removing the cap changes the mineral economy (destroyed enemies
  return ~everything they absorbed, plus a little), which can fill the hold
  faster and yield more power-ups. **Mitigation:** the increase is bounded
  (≤ ~1 mineral per kill on average, plus rounding) and remains tunable.
- **Risk:** renaming persisted-rule keys could silently reset a designer's
  custom values. **Mitigation:** version-aware migration plus tests proving
  legacy configs migrate to defaults and current configs round-trip.
- **Risk:** `Math.round` ties round toward `+∞`; harmless here because the
  bonus is always positive and non-tied values dominate.
- **Scope creep (out of scope):** changes to scatter radius, asteroid drop
  counts, collection, HUD or audio/visual juice. Record separately as linked
  work items if raised.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Which exact formula should replace the current 25–50 % rule?
  (A: `round(collected × random(0.25, 1.25))`; B: literal
  `round(collected + random(0.25, 1.25))`; C: other)
  — **Answer (operator, interactive):** *"B"* — add a random 0.25–1.25 to the
  collected count, then round to the nearest integer.
- **Q:** Should the drop still never exceed the collected count?
  (A: keep the cap; B: remove the cap)
  — **Answer (operator, interactive):** *"B"* — remove the cap; a destroyed
  enemy may drop more minerals than it collected.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUCST4M7008O9CX** – Pluggable power-up choice strategy and permanent-effect support (completed)
- **AH-0MUH1LEDQ0064J78** – [test-failure] PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — asteroid integration > AC6 — the wave clears only after ALL split children are destroyed (no stall, no early clear) — failing test (completed)
- **AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V** – Add particle-based explosion VFX for enemy and player deaths (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: absorbed, absorption, acceptance, add, adding (+272 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mubvgi62004ed9q, 0muhmt5jc004wrsb, absorbed, absorption, add (+254 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: absorbed, add, adding, already, always (+235 more)

# Intake Brief — Show the level name in the level/wave progress label

## Problem statement

The difficulty-curves CSV defines a human-readable `levelName` per level
(`Entry`, `Descent`, `The Core`, `Firestorm`, `Predictable Death`; GDD §3.2),
and `WaveManager.levelName` already exposes the active level's name. The player
never sees it: the level/wave progress label shown in both the centred
transition banner and the persistent HUD readout is purely numeric
(`Level N of 5, Wave M of K`). Players therefore get no thematic cue about
which level (and which escalating challenge) they are in.

## Users

- **Player** — *"As a player, I want the current level's theme name shown in
  the on-screen level/wave label so I know which level I am in and that the
  challenge is escalating."*
- **Designer** — *"As a designer, when I author `levelName` in the
  difficulty-curves CSV (or in the static `LEVELS`), that name should appear in
  the game without further code changes."*

## Existing state

- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` carries `levelName` per `(level, wave)` row;
  the loader validates it as required (`src/core/csv.ts`) and maps it to
  `LevelDefinition.name` (`src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts`).
- `WaveManager.levelName` (`src/waves/WaveManager.ts:151`) returns
  `currentLevel()?.name ?? ''`.
- `PlayScene._progressLabel()` returns `Level N of 5, Wave M of K` (or `Boss`)
  and feeds **both** the persistent HUD readout (`_refreshHudText()`) and the
  centred banner (`_updateTransitionBanner()` on wave transitions,
  `_announceLevel()` at level start). It is therefore the single place to
  change for both surfaces.
- `_announceLevel()` is called at run start and on a `levelCleared` transition;
  wave transitions call `_updateTransitionBanner()`. With the new label sourced
  from `_progressLabel()`, both paths display the level name automatically.
- The banner is **PlayScene-only** — no gym scene renders the campaign
  level/wave label, so no gym↔game parity change is expected (the campaign is a
  game-only concept). This will be confirmed during implementation.

## Desired change (confirmed by producer)

Include the active level's theme name in the shared level/wave progress label,
so it appears in **every** wave's banner **and** in the persistent HUD readout
for the whole level. Confirmed format (operator example):
`Level 1: Entry, Wave: 1 of 2` — i.e.
`Level <N>: <Name>, Wave: <M> of <K>`. The boss encounter keeps its current
`Boss` label.

Producer decisions:

- **Q1 format (answer):** `Level 1: Entry, Wave: 1 of 2`.
- **Q2 frequency (answer b):** show the name on **every** wave in the level.
- **Q3 persistence (answer b):** also add the name to the persistent HUD readout.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Level name in the label:** The shared level/wave progress label
  contains the active level's theme name; with the example campaign it reads
  `Level 1: Entry, Wave: 1 of 2` at run start.
- [ ] **AC2 — Shown on every wave and in the HUD:** The name appears on every
  wave's transition banner (not just the level's first wave) **and** in the
  persistent HUD readout for the whole level.
- [ ] **AC3 — CSV-backed source of truth:** With sequenced waves enabled the
  displayed name is the CSV `levelName`; with the toggle off (static `LEVELS`)
  it is the corresponding `LevelDefinition.name`. A test exercises both paths.
- [ ] **AC4 — Boss unchanged:** The boss encounter still shows `Boss` (no
  numeric level and no name).
- [ ] **AC5 — Graceful fallback:** When the active level has an empty/missing
  name, the label falls back to a name-free numeric form (no blank name, no
  crash). Tested.
- [ ] **AC6 — Banner remains transient:** The banner still hides within the
  existing `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS` (~1.5 s) window
  (AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN behaviour preserved).
- [ ] **AC7 — Tests:** New/updated tests in `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`
  (gameHarness) cover AC1–AC6. The existing
  `AH-0MU7JTEY3004EXR2 AC1/AC2/AC4` expectations (which assert
  `Level N of 5, Wave M of K`) are updated to the new label format
  deliberately in the same change.
- [ ] **AC8 — Docs:** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §3.2 / HUD notes and any
  relevant code comments are updated to describe the level-name label.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** All
  related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Change `_progressLabel()` once so the banner and HUD cannot diverge (single
  source of truth).
- Reuse the existing banner plumbing (`_showBanner`, `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS`);
  no new overlay system.
- Must not regress AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN (transient banner). The
  AH-0MU7JTEY3004EXR2 label-format tests are intentionally updated.
- UK English in all user-facing copy and code comments.
- No gym-parity code change unless a gym is found to render the same label.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_progressLabel()` (add `wm.levelName`), used by
  `_refreshHudText()` and `_updateTransitionBanner()` / `_announceLevel()`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — update AH-0MU7JTEY3004EXR2 expectations and
  add AC1–AC6 tests.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — already exposes `levelName`; no change expected.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §3.2 / HUD description.

## Related work

- **AH-0MU7JTEY3004EXR2** — Show level/wave progress as `Level N of 5, Wave M of K` (completed): introduced the shared `_progressLabel()` used by both the HUD and banner; this item extends its format with the level name.
- **AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN** — Level transition banner persists for the whole wave (completed): introduced the transient `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS` banner; this item must preserve it.
- **AH-0MUH6LEYY0054E63** — Wire the runtime auto-sequencer into the game's wave generation (completed): introduced the CSV-backed campaign and `levelName` plumbing.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts:151` — existing `levelName` accessor (reused, not changed).

### Automated related-work report

See the `
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT7QQGBU008V4R0** – Write the Game Design Document (completed)
- **AH-0MUGCNZNE002D7QJ** – Implement — PlayScene asteroid spawner integration (completed)
- **AH-0MUA8BGE0006UAU4** – SettingsScene: key-binding remapping + reset to defaults (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muh6leyy0054e63, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+223 more)
- `README.md` — matched: ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance, accessor (+222 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0muh6leyy0054e63, ac1, ac4, accessor, active (+211 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the boss encounter has no level name and keeps the literal
  `Boss` label; the GDD's `AI Throne` boss theme is not part of the campaign
  `LEVELS` and is out of scope. *Mitigation:* AC4.
- **Risk — existing test contract changes:** the label format change
  invalidates the `AH-0MU7JTEY3004EXR2` expectations. Mitigation: update those
  assertions deliberately in the same change (AC7).
- **Risk — scope creep:** adding the name to the pause menu, game-over screen,
  or leaderboard is out of scope; record any such ideas as linked work items
  rather than expanding this item.
- **Failure mode:** a level with an empty name (e.g. a custom campaign) must not
  produce a blank/awkward label — AC5.
- **Note:** the operator's example writes `Wave: 1 of 2` (colon after "Wave").
  The implementation matches the operator example exactly; the exact separator
  is pinned by the AC7 test.

## Open Questions

None — all three presentation questions were answered by the producer; see the
Appendix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (presentation format)** — Answer (operator): `Level 1: Entry, Wave: 1 of 2`.
  Source: interactive reply. Status: resolved.
- **Q2 (frequency)** — Answer (operator): (b) every wave in the level. Source:
  interactive reply. Status: resolved.
- **Q3 (persistent HUD)** — Answer (operator): (b) also add the name to the
  persistent HUD readout. Source: interactive reply. Status: resolved.
- Q: Where does the level name come from? — Answer (research, no operator
  input needed): the difficulty-curves CSV `levelName` column, surfaced as
  `LevelDefinition.name` and `WaveManager.levelName`. Source:
  `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`, `src/core/csv.ts`, `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts`.
- Q: Does this need a gym change? — Answer (research): no gym scene renders the
  campaign level/wave label, so no parity change is expected. Source:
  `src/scenes/gym/`.

# Test: additive mineral re-drop rule

Test-first task for AH-0MULUOZQP009GRWX (parent AC1–AC4).

## Goal
Pin the new additive re-drop rule **before** implementation so the formula,
the removed cap and the game/gym parity are provably one shared contract.

## Required coverage
- `BaseEnemy.mineralRedropCount(rng)` returns `Math.round(collected + 0.25)` at
  `rng() = 0` and `Math.round(collected + 1.25)` as `rng() → 1`, for several
  collected counts (e.g. 1, 2, 3, 5, 10).
- The bonus is drawn exactly once per call from the injected rng (a counting
  stub rng observes one draw; the same seed ⇒ the same count).
- No upper cap: for `N = 1` and `N = 2` the maximum re-drop
  (`round(N + 1.25)`) exceeds `N`, and for every N the result is never below
  `round(N + 0.25)`.
- Empty enemy unchanged: `mineralRedropCount` returns `0` when
  `mineralCount <= 0`, regardless of rng.
- `resolveMineralKillDrops` (shared rule) spawns exactly
  `mineralRedropCount(rng)` scattered minerals at the death site for a
  non-asteroid enemy, and keeps the small/large/medium asteroid branches
  unchanged.
- The repo-wide duplicate-body guard in
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` still passes (single
  shared definition).

## Acceptance Criteria
- New/updated tests cover every bullet under Required coverage.
- Assertions are deterministic (seeded or stub rng; no `Math.random`).
- Tests fail against the current 25–50 % capped implementation and pass once
  the tunable-rename and formula implementation tasks land.
- The touched test files run under `npm test`.

## Key Files
- `src/entities/__tests__/BaseEnemy.minerals.test.ts` — rewrite the re-drop distribution tests for the new formula and removed cap.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.test.ts` — expected counts at the rng extremes.
- `src/entities/Harvester.test.ts` — Harvester re-drop test.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — non-asteroid re-drop test (remove the never-exceed assertion).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — parity guard stays green.

# Test: renamed re-drop bonus tunables and v3 migration

Test-first task for AH-0MULUOZQP009GRWX (parent AC5).

## Goal
Pin the renamed bonus tunables and the schema-v3 migration **before** the
rules implementation changes, so persisted-config behaviour cannot regress.

## Required coverage
- `DEFAULT_RULES.mineralRedropBonusMin` = 0.25 and
  `DEFAULT_RULES.mineralRedropBonusMax` = 1.25.
- `saveRules` / `loadRules` round-trip custom `mineralRedropBonusMin`/`Max`
  values, including a value above 1 (e.g. 1.5).
- Invalid values fall back to the default: negative, `NaN` and non-number are
  rejected; zero is accepted (non-negative coercion).
- Legacy migration: a persisted config stamped `version: 1`, `version: 2`, or
  with no version loads with the bonus tunables reset to the new defaults and
  does not carry stale `mineralRedropFraction*` values.
- A current schema-v3 config round-trips unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Tests cover the defaults, save/load round-trip, invalid-value fallback and
  legacy v1/v2 migration.
- Assertions use the new `mineralRedropBonusMin`/`Max` names and prove the old
  `mineralRedropFraction*` keys are absent from loaded output.

## Key Files
- `src/core/rules.test.ts` — defaults, round-trip, invalid fallback and legacy migration for the renamed tunables.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — read for the contract (implementation lands in the sibling task).

# Rename re-drop tunables and bump rules schema to v3

Implementation task for AH-0MULUOZQP009GRWX (parent AC5).

## Goal
Rename the re-drop tunables to describe the new additive semantics, widen the
accepted range, and migrate persisted legacy configs.

## Minimal implementation
- `src/core/rules.ts`: rename `mineralRedropFractionMin`/`Max` to
  `mineralRedropBonusMin`/`Max` on `GameRules`, `DEFAULT_RULES`,
  `cloneDefaultRules` and `loadRules`.
- New defaults/constants: `DEFAULT_MINERAL_REDROP_BONUS_MIN = 0.25` and
  `DEFAULT_MINERAL_REDROP_BONUS_MAX = 1.25`.
- Replace `coerceFraction` for these fields with a non-negative finite
  coercion that accepts values ≥ 0 (including > 1) and rejects
  negative/`NaN`/non-number with the default. Keep `coerceFraction` only if it
  is still used elsewhere; otherwise remove it.
- Bump `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION` to 3. Treat v1/v2 (and missing/corrupt version)
  as legacy and reset the bonus tunables to the new defaults in `loadRules` —
  do not carry stale fraction values forward.
- Update the JSDoc/comments describing the tunables and the schema history.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The tunables are named `mineralRedropBonusMin`/`Max`, default to 0.25/1.25,
  and persist/load with corrupt-value fallback.
- Legacy v1/v2 configs migrate to the new defaults without carrying stale
  fraction values; current v3 configs round-trip.
- The tests from the test-first tunables task pass.

## Key Files
- `src/core/rules.ts` — renamed tunables, new defaults, coercion, schema v3 and migration.
- `src/core/rules.test.ts` — driven by the test-first task.

# Implement additive mineral re-drop formula

Implementation task for AH-0MULUOZQP009GRWX (parent AC1–AC4).

## Goal
Replace the 25–50 % floored/clamped re-drop with an additive random bonus
rounded to the nearest integer, and remove the upper cap.

## Minimal implementation
- `BaseEnemy.mineralRedropCount(rng)`: keep the `_mineralCount <= 0 → 0`
  guard; draw the bonus once as
  `rules.mineralRedropBonusMin + rng() * (rules.mineralRedropBonusMax - rules.mineralRedropBonusMin)`;
  return `Math.round(this._mineralCount + bonus)` — one rng draw, no clamp to
  the collected count.
- Update the method JSDoc to describe the additive bonus and nearest-integer
  rounding (drop the "never exceeding" claim).
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts`: update the module-header rule
  description to the additive bonus. Logic is unchanged — it still delegates
  to `mineralRedropCount` and remains the single shared definition.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `mineralRedropCount` matches `round(collected + random(0.25, 1.25))` with
  exactly one injected draw and no upper cap; empty enemies still return 0.
- The shared rule remains the single implementation consumed by `PlayScene`
  and every gym (no divergent copy).
- The tests from the test-first re-drop task pass.

## Key Files
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — new `mineralRedropCount` formula and updated JSDoc.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` — rule description in the module header (logic unchanged).

# Documentation update and full-suite verification

Final task for AH-0MULUOZQP009GRWX (parent AC6, AC7).

## Goal
Document the additive re-drop rule, the removed cap and the renamed tunables,
then prove the whole project is green.

## Minimal implementation
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`: update §4.1 E7 and §4.4.1 to state the
  additive `round(collected + random(0.25, 1.25))` bonus, the removed upper
  cap and the renamed `mineralRedropBonusMin`/`Max` (0.25/1.25) tunables;

# Intake Brief — More enemy variety in the first 3-4 waves

**Headline:** Make the campaign's first four waves (Level 1 waves 1–2 and Level 2 waves 1–2) build with the `dynamic` generation mode so each run opens on a varied mix of existing enemy archetypes instead of repeated Scouts — while preserving the no-enemy-fire onboarding boundary and the retuned-campaign difficulty ramp.

## Seed description

There is a lot of repition in the first few waves, introduce more enemy variety.

## Problem statement

The shipped campaign opens with the same enemy for three waves in a row: L1W1 `scout x6`, L1W2 `scout x8`, L2W1 `scout x8`, then L2W2 `diver x8`. Levels 1–3 are generation mode `fixed`, so they reuse the hand-authored static `LEVELS` waves verbatim and never vary between runs. The opening is therefore repetitive and under-exposes the enemy roster.

## Users / user stories

- **As a player**, I want the opening waves to feature different enemy types rather than the same Scouts, so the first minutes feel varied and teach more of the roster.
- **As a player**, I want the opening waves to vary between runs, so repeat playthroughs feel fresh.
- **As a designer**, I want the added variety to preserve the onboarding difficulty ramp and the no-enemy-fire boundary (GDD §2.4/§3.2), so early play stays approachable and consistent with the rest of the campaign.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Dynamic, non-firing opening.** The first four campaign waves (L1W1, L1W2, L2W1, L2W2) have `generation: dynamic` and remain non-firing (`shootEnabled === false`). *Verification:* assert `generation` and `shootEnabled` on `buildSequencedLevels()` output; the fire boundary for levels 1–3 is unchanged.
- **AC2 — Real variety.** Across the four waves at the default seed, at least three distinct existing enemy archetypes appear, and no two of the four waves share an identical composition. *Verification:* unit test on the built campaign.
- **AC3 — Per-run variation with reproducibility.** The four dynamic waves differ across at least two distinct run seeds, while each seed reproduces its campaign exactly (dynamic is a pure function of curve, pool and seed; `curve`/`fixed` waves stay seed-independent). *Verification:* build with ≥2 seeds and assert variation plus same-seed equality.
- **AC4 — No regression of the retuned campaign.** The first four waves are non-degenerate: no asteroid-only wave and no 1-count wave in levels 1–3; the AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K regression pins still pass (no-degeneracy, non-decreasing targets within and across levels, strictly rising aggregated difficulty, fire boundary held). *Verification:* existing/updated regression suite.
- **AC5 — Defaults and seed agree.** `defaultDifficultyCurves()` and `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` both mark L1W1..L2W2 `dynamic` with matching retuned targets, and every other wave's mode/target is unchanged. *Verification:* config-store and CSV seed tests.
- **AC6 — Testing/validation.** New or updated unit/integration tests cover mode dispatch, seed variation and reproducibility, the non-degeneracy guarantee and the difficulty ramp; the full project test suite passes.
- **AC7 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md`, the GDD (§3.2 Level 1 description and the default-campaign note) and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

## Constraints

- **Existing archetypes only** (producer decision 1→2a): re-mix `scout`, `diver`, `tank`, `swarm`, `phaser` (and the roaming `asteroid`); do **not** add or invent new enemy archetypes.
- **Dynamic and non-firing** (producer decision 3b): the four waves regenerate per run from their curve and seed, but levels 1–3 must not fire (GDD §2.4/§3.2 boundary).
- **Must not regress AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K**: no asteroid-only and no 1-count wave in levels 1–3; targets non-decreasing; aggregated difficulty strictly rising; fire boundary held.
- **Determinism contract** (AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT): `curve`/`fixed` waves are seed-independent; `dynamic` waves are a pure function of (curve, candidate pool, seed).
- **Gym↔game parity** (AGENTS.md): the campaign builder is shared core; any gym that exercises it must stay consistent.
- UK English in all code comments, tests and documentation.

## Existing state

- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` marks levels 1–3 `fixed`, levels 4–5 `curve`, and L5W2 `dynamic`.
- `src/core/configStore.ts`: `DEFAULT_FIXED_LEVELS = {1,2,3}`, `DEFAULT_MODE_OVERRIDES = {5:{2:'dynamic'}}`, `DEFAULT_TARGET_OVERRIDES = {4:[16,24,28], 5:[45,62]}`. `defaultDifficultyCurves()` emits each wave's mode as `DEFAULT_MODE_OVERRIDES[level]?.[wave] ?? (fixed ? 'fixed' : 'curve')`, so per-wave override of a `fixed` level is already supported with no new mechanism.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` dispatches per wave on `generation`. A `dynamic` wave applies a seed-derived ±`DYNAMIC_TARGET_JITTER` (20) shift to its target before re-sequencing; `fixed` reuses the static `LEVELS` wave verbatim.
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`: `defaultCandidatePool()` is every archetype except `harvester`, with `count` as the only adjustable field; `DEFAULT_TOLERANCE = 10`; multi-group composition is on by default.
- Regression pin: `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` → describe "Retuned default campaign (AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K)".

### Feasibility finding (evidence)

Making the four waves `dynamic` with the **current** targets (3.01, 6.01, 7.66, 9.3) and the default pool reintroduces the exact degeneracy AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K removed. With the ±20 dynamic jitter the sequencer emits `asteroid x1` (or another 1-count group) for most seeds, and occasionally wildly inconsistent waves (`phaser x12`, `swarm x45`). Non-firing difficulty is nearly flat in enemy count — `scout x1 = 5.34` … `x6 = 5.89`, `asteroid x1 = 8.62`, `diver x1 = 11.55`, `swarm x1 = 12.76`, `tank x1 = 15.10`, `phaser x1 = 18.28` — so the default pool has no low-difficulty band that yields varied, non-degenerate waves. The early `curve` targets are also artificially low (roughly half the measured level score), which compounds this. The mode dispatch itself needs no new mechanism.

## Desired change

- Mark L1W1, L1W2, L2W1 and L2W2 as `dynamic` in both `defaultDifficultyCurves()` and the seed CSV (add them to `DEFAULT_MODE_OVERRIDES`); leave the rest of levels 1–3 `fixed`.
- Resolve the degeneracy so the four dynamic waves are varied and non-degenerate at every seed — the mechanism is a **plan-stage decision** (see Open decision).
- Retune the four waves' targets so the opening ramp stays smooth and aggregated difficulty still rises from level 1 upward.
- Update the GDD (Level 1 "Scout V-formations" wording and the default-campaign note), README/design docs and code comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — L1W1..L2W2 → `dynamic`; retuned targets.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `DEFAULT_MODE_OVERRIDES` (add the four waves) and retuned early targets in `defaultDifficultyCurves()`.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — likely seam for a curated early-wave candidate pool and/or minimum-count floor (mechanism TBD at plan).
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — candidate-pool/tolerance/jitter tuning if the chosen mechanism requires it.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts`, `src/core/configStore.test.ts`, `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — update/extend the regression pins and add variety/determinism assertions.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §3.2, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `README.md` — document the dynamic opening and the curation.

## Open decision (resolve at planning)

How to make low-difficulty dynamic waves varied and non-degenerate **without new archetypes**. Recommended approach: give the opening waves a **curated early-game candidate pool** (e.g. `scout`/`diver`/`swarm`/`tank`, excluding `asteroid`/`boss`/`phaser`) with a **minimum-count floor** (count ≥ ~4) and retune their targets into a narrow ascending band, so the sequencer selects a different light archetype per wave and the seed jitter varies the mix across runs while the no-degeneracy regression still passes. Alternatives: reduce/parameterise `DYNAMIC_TARGET_JITTER`; tighten the sequencer tolerance; or compose the opening waves from multiple groups. Whichever is chosen must satisfy AC1–AC5.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K** — Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign for playability (completed) — established the no-degeneracy/ramp regression this change must preserve.
- **AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT** — Per-wave generation modes: `curve`, `fixed` and dynamic runtime regeneration (completed) — the mode dispatch and the determinism contract.
- **AH-0MUJSUTLA006Q8E1** — Enable sequenced wave generation by default with a mixed-mode initial campaign (completed) — the shipped mixed-mode campaign.
- **AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123** — Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen (completed) — asteroids are a roaming hazard, not a wave group.
- **AH-0MUH6LEYY0054E63** / **AH-0MUITRZZE000OYQE** — difficulty-curve / runtime auto-sequencer programme (completed).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — degeneracy recurrence (high, evidenced):** dynamic + low targets yields asteroid-only/1-count waves. *Mitigation:* AC4 regression plus the Open-decision mechanism.
- **Risk — difficulty-ramp inversion:** raising early targets to avoid degeneracy can push levels 1–2 towards level 4. *Mitigation:* keep the four targets in an ascending band below L4W1 (16) and assert rising aggregated difficulty (AC4).
- **Risk — seed jitter is erratic at low targets:** ±20 is large relative to a ~5–15 target band. *Mitigation:* narrow the band/curate the pool, or reduce/parameterise the jitter (plan decision).
- **Risk — scope creep:** adding new archetypes, reworking later levels, or changing global difficulty tuning is out of scope; record such ideas as linked work items.
- **Assumption (producer, 1a):** "first 3-4 waves" = the campaign's first four waves (L1W1, L1W2, L2W1, L2W2).
- **Assumption (producer, 2a):** re-mix existing archetypes only; no new archetypes.
- **Assumption (producer, 3b):** the four waves are `dynamic` (per-run variation) and non-firing.
- **Assumption (to confirm at plan):** the degeneracy mechanism is resolved per the Open decision; implementation may add a per-wave candidate-pool / count-floor seam.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q (round 1): "Scope — which waves are 'the first 3-4 waves'?" — Answer (producer): **"(a)"** = the first 3-4 waves of the whole campaign (L1W1, L1W2, L2W1, L2W2), including Level 1. Source: interactive reply, this session (work-item comment `AH-C0MUPJFJ0Z007UOA6`).
- Q (round 1): "Archetype source — re-mix existing enemies or add new archetypes?" — Answer (producer): **"(a)"** = re-mix the existing archetypes only (scout, diver, tank, swarm, phaser, asteroid). Source: comment `AH-C0MUPJFL95001OIUF`.
- Q (round 1): "Determinism and fire boundary — should early waves stay fixed and non-firing?" — Answer (producer): **"(b)"** = convert the early waves to dynamic so they vary per run but still do not fire. Source: comment `AH-C0MUPJFNXN004MC54`.
- Research (agent): the opening repetition is because levels 1–3 are `fixed`; the no-degeneracy and fire-boundary constraints come from AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K; dynamic + current low targets is degenerate (empirical finding above). Source: repo inspection, this session.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUGQCMNA0061J4A** – Replace Player.tryFire per-weapon cooldowns with phase-locked beat scheduling (completed)
- **AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123** – Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen (completed)
- **AH-0MUJRW0GV007JK6S** – Campaign roaming Harvester spawns (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: create, enemy, first, introduce, lot (+2 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: create, enemy, first, introduce, lot (+2 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: create, enemy, first, lot, there (+1 more)

---

## Plan (decomposed 2026-10-01)

**Plan summary.** Resolve the intake Open decision with a measured spike, then
implement the dynamic, varied, non-firing opening as a test-first vertical
slice, and document it. Existing archetypes only; levels 1–3 stay non-firing;
the AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K regression pins must keep passing.

**Approval gate:** not required — effort Small and risk Medium do not trigger a
human plan-approval pause (`plan_helpers.py plan-approval-gate` returned
`request_approval: false`).

### Features (children, in dependency order)

1. **Spike: validate dynamic opening-wave sequencing mechanism** — AH-0MUQ523AJ0064PR3
   *(task, high, Small/Medium)*. Determine and record the concrete mechanism
   and parameters (curated early candidate pool, minimum-count floor,
   parameterised jitter, four retuned ascending targets) that make L1W1..L2W2
   varied and non-degenerate across a seed sweep. Deliverable: decision record +
   parameter set. No dependencies.
2. **Tests: dynamic opening variety, determinism and regression** —
   AH-0MUQ523A90028N9B *(task, high, Small/Low)*. Add failing-first tests for the
   parent AC1–AC6: dynamic + non-firing opening, ≥3 distinct archetypes / four
   distinct compositions at the default seed, seed variation with same-seed
   reproducibility, no-degeneracy across seeds, unchanged regression pins, and
   defaults/CSV agreement. Depends on (1).
3. **Implement dynamic, varied non-firing opening waves** —
   AH-0MUQ5262M009UFLU *(feature, high, Small/Medium)*. Apply the spike
   mechanism in the shared core; mark L1W1..L2W2 `dynamic` in
   `defaultDifficultyCurves()` and `difficulty-curves.csv` with matching
   retuned targets; keep gym↔game parity; make the tests green; build + full
   suite pass. Depends on (1) and (2).
4. **Document the dynamic, varied opening** — AH-0MUQ52620006N3SE
   *(docs, medium, Small/Low)*. Update GDD §3.2 (Level 1 wording and the
   default-campaign note), `README.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
   §9.6 and code comments; remove stale Scout-only / levels 1–3 fully-fixed
   claims. Depends on (3).

### Dependency edges

- Tests (2) → Spike (1)
- Implement (3) → Spike (1), Tests (2)
- Document (4) → Implement (3)

### Vertical-slice phasing

Each phase is a vertical slice for the work it covers. The spike cuts through
design + measurement + decision; the test slice encodes the observable
acceptance contract across the campaign builder and config/CSV surfaces; the
implementation slice applies the mechanism end-to-end (shared core, defaults,
CSV seed, comments) and makes the acceptance tests green; the docs slice
propagates the shipped behaviour to the player- and designer-facing
documentation. Between phases, re-read the next child's description and update
it if the spike's findings change its parameters or scope.

### Open decision resolution

The intake Open decision ("how to keep low-difficulty dynamic waves varied and
non-degenerate without new archetypes") is delegated to child (1). The
implemented mechanism is whatever the spike validates; the intake-recommended
curated early pool + minimum-count floor + retuned ascending band (likely with
a reduced/parameterised jitter) is the starting point, not a commitment.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-01 — Initial plan: 4 children created (spike, tests, implement,
  docs), 4 dependency edges wired, effort/risk estimated for every child.
  Parent intake Appendix reviewed; no new interview questions were required
  (all product decisions already answered in intake). Mechanism deferred to the
  spike child per the intake Open decision.

### Appendix addendum (plan round)

- No new clarifying questions were asked in the plan round: the intake Appendix
  already resolves the product decisions (scope = first four campaign waves;
  existing archetypes only; dynamic and non-firing). The one remaining
  decision — the non-degeneracy mechanism — is explicitly a plan-stage
  engineering decision per the intake brief and is delegated to the spike child
  (AH-0MUQ523AJ0064PR3), whose acceptance criteria require measured evidence.

campaign (AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K) must not regress.

## Scope

- Apply the spike's mechanism in the shared core: per-wave (or early-wave)
  curated candidate pool, minimum-count floor and parameterised jitter, as
  decided.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — add the four waves to `DEFAULT_MODE_OVERRIDES`
  and add their retuned targets to `DEFAULT_TARGET_OVERRIDES` (or equivalent).
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — mark L1W1..L2W2 `dynamic` with the
  matching retuned targets.
- Any required seam in `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` /
  `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`.
- Update code comments describing the curation and the determinism contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- L1W1..L2W2 are `dynamic` in both `defaultDifficultyCurves()` and
  `difficulty-curves.csv`, with identical retuned targets, and every other
  wave's mode and target is unchanged (including the L5W2 dynamic wave).
- The four opening waves are non-firing (`shootEnabled === false`); the
  levels 1–3 fire boundary is unchanged.
- At the default seed the opening uses at least three distinct archetypes and
  no two of the four compositions are identical; across at least two seeds the
  compositions differ; the same seed reproduces exactly.
- No opening wave (levels 1–3) is asteroid-only or a 1-count group; targets
  stay ascending and below the L4W1 target (16); the aggregated level
  difficulty strictly rises from level 1 upward.
- The implementation lives once in the shared core, so the game's
  `buildSequencedLevels` path and the gym preview path stay consistent
  (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity); any intentional divergence is documented in the
  work item and a code comment.
- All tests from the test child pass, the full project test suite passes, and
  `npm run build` (typecheck + build) passes.
- Code comments are updated and use UK English.

- **Parent AC1 — Dynamic, non-firing opening** (covered): L1W1..L2W2 have `generation: dynamic` and remain non-firing (`shootEnabled === false`) on `buildSequencedLevels()` output.
- **Parent AC2 — Real variety** (covered): at least three distinct existing enemy archetypes appear across the four waves at the default seed with no two identical compositions.
- **Parent AC3 — Per-run variation with reproducibility** (covered): the four dynamic waves differ across at least two run seeds and each seed reproduces its campaign exactly.
- **Parent AC4 — No regression of the retuned campaign** (covered): no asteroid-only wave and no 1-count wave in levels 1–3; the AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K pins (non-decreasing targets within/across levels, strictly rising aggregated difficulty, fire boundary held) still pass.
- **Parent AC5 — Defaults and seed agree** (covered): `defaultDifficultyCurves()` and `difficulty-curves.csv` both mark L1W1..L2W2 dynamic with matching retuned targets; every other wave's mode and target is unchanged.
- **Parent AC6 — Testing/validation** (covered): the full project test suite passes and `npm run build` (typecheck + build) passes.

## Deliverables

- Committed implementation with tests green.
- A commit that references AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B, recorded in a work-item comment
  with the commit hash.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the spike child (parameters) and the test child (red tests).

## Notes

- Build → test → commit order; never reverse.
- Do not change later levels, add archetypes, or alter global difficulty
  tuning (out of scope).
